svg.text: The gaps are not empty regions of space — they are orbits that Jupiter makes untenable.
predicted from a = a_J (q/p)²⃗³, with no reference to the data
A body in a Kirkwood gap gets a kick from Jupiter at the same orbital phase every time, so its
eccentricity grows until it crosses a planet’s orbit and is scattered or destroyed. Emptying a gap
takes a few million years — which is also how the near-Earth population is continuously resupplied.
What DELIVERS bodies into the gaps is the Yarkovsky effect: a thermal recoil of ~10⁻⁴ AU per Myr.
